bull_bear.body:
- Over five decades of experience manufacturing paper maker's felts, recognised as a reliable supplier for high-speed paper machines in India and select export markets
- Consistent product quality, technical expertise and competitive pricing that management credits for strong customer relationships
- Recent successes in critical high-speed applications in India, Russia and Brazil, which management says strengthened its market position
- In-house R&D department active in product and process improvement/development and in monitoring the Company's Effluent Treatment Plants
- Wind Turbine Generators already installed and used for captive power consumption, reducing exposure to purchased energy
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Import-led pricing pressure on the domestic paper value chain — The MD&A industry review flags increasing imports from ASEAN countries and China as a driver of pricing pressure on domestic manufacturers, which flows through to demand and pricing for machine clothing supplied to Indian mills.
- Intense competition from domestic and overseas suppliers, especially multinationals — Listed under Threats: competition in price-sensitive segments continues to exert pressure on margins, and rapid technological advancements by multinational competitors are named as a major industry challenge for a company that acknowledges limited global brand visibility in certain premium applications.
- Dependence on imported specialty raw materials and raw-material price volatility — Named under Weaknesses (dependence on imported specialty raw materials) and Threats (volatility in raw material prices); the industry review also cites rising raw material costs as an industry-level challenge.
- Foreign exchange exposure — Exchange-rate volatility is named both as an industry challenge and under Threats. The Company has two-way FX exposure — Annexure 'A' reports FY26 foreign exchange earnings of Rs. 1177.34 Lakhs against outgo of Rs. 1252.65 Lakhs — and the forward-looking disclaimer explicitly cites exchange rate change as a factor that could alter outcomes.
- Rising energy costs and reliance on power-intensive manufacturing — Rising energy costs appear both as an industry challenge and under Weaknesses. The Company mitigates partially through Wind Turbine Generators used for captive consumption, but made no capital investment in energy-conservation equipment during the year.
- Environmental compliance burden — Environmental compliance requirements are named as an industry challenge; the Secretarial Audit records the Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981, Environment Protection Act 1986 and Water Cess Act 1977 as specifically applicable to the Company, and the R&D function is tasked with monitoring the Effluent Treatment Plants.
- Operational scalability and automation gap constraining margins — Management's own SWOT Weaknesses state that further improvements are required in manufacturing automation, process optimisation and operational scalability to enhance productivity and margins — a structural constraint acknowledged by the Board rather than an external shock.
- Execution and structural uncertainty around the proposed Felt demerger and promoter family settlement — Following a Family Settlement Agreement executed on 29 April 2026 between the BUP and NUP promoter families (disclosed to BSE under LODR Regulations 30/30A), the Board granted in-principle approval for demerger of the Felt business into a separate legal entity, subject to NCLT and other approvals, and segregated the Felt and Residual businesses under separate director oversight. Cross-bundle: the FSA and demerger detail is in the Boards' Report 'Material Changes and Commitment' item present in every bundle.
- Concentrated founder-family control and key-person dependence — The four executive directors — Chairman & Managing Director, Managing Director and two Executive Directors — are related to each other and together hold roughly 45.7% of equity (14.20%, 13.73%, 8.79% and 9.01% per the Corporate Governance shareholding-of-directors table); the Boards' Report notes the Risk Management Committee provisions are not applicable to the Company.

business.body: The Company manufactures paper maker's felts, i.e. technical textiles used as machine clothing on paper machines, and supplies them to paper mills running high-speed machines in India and in export markets. outlook.body:
- Segregate the Felt (technical textiles) business from the Residual business with separate director oversight for each vertical, ahead of a proposed demerger of the Felt business into a separate legal entity subject to NCLT and other approvals
- Deepen presence in critical high-speed paper-machine applications, building on wins in India, Russia and Brazil, and in export markets alongside the domestic base
- Target growth in packaging, tissue and specialty paper segments with advanced machine clothing products, including seamed felts
- Improve manufacturing automation, process optimisation and operational scalability, which management identifies as required to lift productivity and margins
- Simplify the group structure — the Company divested its entire shareholding in Dinesh Remedies Ltd. during FY26 while continuing to fund wholly owned subsidiaries Fernway Technologies Ltd. and Stellent Chemicals Industries Ltd.
- Continue R&D on product and process improvement/development and on monitoring of the Company's Effluent Treatment Plants
- Continue using wind power for captive consumption via already-installed Wind Turbine Generators as an alternate energy source
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report discloses no capacity addition, plant commissioning or expansion project. The only structural change described is corporate rather than physical: the Board granted in-principle approval to demerge the Felt (technical textiles) business into a separate legal entity, subject to NCLT and other approvals, and in the interim approved segregation of the Felt and Residual businesses with directors assigned to oversee each vertical separately. On the group side the Company divested its entire 55.52% shareholding in Dinesh Remedies Ltd. on 3 September 2025, and subscribed on a rights basis to 7,07,200 0.01% Optionally Convertible Non-Cumulative Preference Shares of Rs. 10/- each of wholly owned subsidiary Fernway Technologies Ltd. Energy-side, Wind Turbine Generators are already installed for captive consumption and the Boards' Report states there were no capital investments on energy conservation equipment during the year. R&D remains an ongoing in-house activity focused on product and process improvement/development and on monitoring the Company's Effluent Treatment Plants.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian paper industry continues to show steady growth, supported mainly by packaging paper, paperboard, kraft paper and tissue segments
- Indian per-capita paper consumption remains low at approximately 16-18 kgs versus a global average of 57 kgs, which management reads as strong long-term growth potential
- Government initiatives discouraging single-use plastics and increasing focus on sustainable packaging are driving higher demand for paper-based products
- Growth in e-commerce, FMCG, food delivery, pharmaceuticals and organised retail is supporting demand for packaging grades; tissue paper continues to see strong growth on rising hygiene awareness and lifestyle changes
- Expansion of high-speed paper machines and increasing demand for seamed felts are expected to create growth potential in both domestic and export markets, alongside global supply-chain diversification
- Management expects Felts sales turnover to rise in the current financial year, but net profit to remain under pressure from global disruption, which it will strive to mitigate
- FY26 profit fell mainly due to an increase in overhead expenses, per management's overall review of operations
- Headwinds flagged: rising raw material and energy costs, foreign exchange fluctuations, environmental compliance requirements, and rising imports from ASEAN countries and China creating pricing pressure on domestic manufacturers

- Environmental compliance burden — Environmental compliance requirements are named as an industry challenge; the Secretarial Audit records the Water Act 1974, Air Act 1981, Environment Protection Act 1986 and Water Cess Act 1977 as specifically applicable to the Company, and the R&D function is tasked with monitoring the Effluent Treatment Plants.
- Operational scalability and automation gap constraining margins — Management's own SWOT Weaknesses state that further improvements are required in manufacturing automation, process optimisation and operational scalability to enhance productivity and margins — a structural constraint acknowledged by the Board rather than an external shock.
- Execution and structural uncertainty around the proposed Felt demerger and promoter family settlement — Following a Family Settlement Agreement executed on 29 April 2026 between the BUP and NUP promoter families (disclosed to BSE under LODR Regulations 30/30A), the Board granted in-principle approval for demerger of the Felt business into a separate legal entity, subject to NCLT and other approvals, and segregated the Felt and Residual businesses under separate director oversight. Cross-bundle: the FSA and demerger detail is in the Boards' Report 'Material Changes and Commitment' item present in every bundle.
- Concentrated founder-family control and key-person dependence — The four executive directors — Chairman & Managing Director, Managing Director and two Executive Directors — are related to each other and together hold roughly 45.7% of equity (14.20%, 13.73%, 8.79% and 9.01% per the Corporate Governance shareholding-of-directors table); the Boards' Report notes the Risk Management Committee provisions are not applicable to the Company.
